A lot has happened since I took over this subverse not long ago. When I took over it was extremely dead. I posted here asking for input on how you, the users, would like this place to progress. A lot of great suggestions came in through mail, and more posted in comments. Here's what's changed:

To encourage posting, anonymous mode has been turned on. Nobody can link your posts back to you, in any way. This cannot be removed, ever, for the life of the subverse now that it's turned on. If I lose moderation and someone else gains it a year from now, still they cannot remove anonymous mode. I cannot even see as a moderator who is commenting or posting.

Anonymous mode also removes us from /r/all - this will aid in preventing brigaids by SJWs who hate this type of content. If we DO run into an issue with a lot of spam and shit posting, I will start a 5 CCP post minimum. Any user on Voat more than a week should have 5 CCP, but new alts created to spam won't be able to post.

Turning Anonymous mode on also disables upvoats and downvoats on posts, this effectively froze the front page, no posts would ever surpass even posts that had 2 upvoats. Thus, all old posts were removed, I encourage you all to take control and post to your hearts content, now that you can be safe in knowing it can't be traced to your Voat username.

I am going to be an extremely active moderator, and by that I mean primarily deleting links with broken images. I won't police what you post content wise - if it's off topic I'll delete it but if it's objectionable someone can report it to the authorities per Atko's quote in the sidebar. We are not here to play wack-a-mole, if you think it's illegal, report it to your local police. We have no power to prevent illegal activity.

Links from imgur won't be deleted, but be aware that if this subverse gets on someone's radar and they mention it to imgur, imgur could go through and purge all images that are linked to from here. Theoretically.

I would suggest posts to slimger primarily, veuer is also a decent suggestion, but I anticipate a longer lifespan for slimger. I will update this as needed with more content and information.

If looking for content to post please see the link in the sidebar.

A native app is always going to be quicker than rendering a website. The mobile website for Voat is very good, but it's still slow on my crappy Samsung phone, whereas apps aren't.

Voat is far from the fastest website I've ever used, but if it's because of an overloaded server, then an app won't help much (since the server calls which still happen within an app will still take a long time). You'll remove some cached overhead, but that's relatively minimal. An analogy would be like saying "my car is already packed, so it will shorten the drive" even though your car is capped at 15 mph.

The network requests are probably around the same, it's rendering the actual HTML which is the issue. The difference is pretty obvious on my crappy low-end phone, maybe it's not as noticeable on more modern devices.
